contentBlocks.heading: Why a Predicted Grade and a Final Grade Are Not the Same Number
contentBlocks.body:
A predicted grade is a school's informed estimate, based on classwork, mocks and how a student has performed so far. The final grade comes from external moderation against IB's own criteria, under exam conditions, months later. For a Canadian International School Bangalore student sitting a predicted 6 in Economics or Math AI HL, the gap to a final 6, or the risk of a final 5, usually comes down to specific, fixable habits rather than a general lack of ability.

Common gaps: an Economics student who understands the theory but writes essays that drift instead of directly answering the command term; a Math student who solves problems correctly in class but loses time and marks under timed exam conditions; an English or TOK student whose ideas are strong but whose written structure loses the examiner partway through. None of these are content problems in the usual sense. They are performance-under-conditions problems, and they respond to targeted practice rather than more general revision.

This matters for how a family should think about tutoring support. A tutor's job in the months before May or November 2026 is not to re-teach two years of content from the beginning, but to diagnose exactly which of these specific gaps is holding a predicted grade back and work on that directly, with the student's actual recent assessed work as the starting point rather than a generic syllabus checklist.

contentBlocks.heading: The Subjects Bangalore Families Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
Requests connected to Canadian International School Bangalore students concentrate around Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, broadly mirroring what most DP students at ambitious Bangalore schools are taking. Economics comes up often specifically for essay technique: students who know the theory but lose marks because an answer does not directly evaluate against the command term, or drifts into description where analysis was asked for.

English writing support is a recurring, specific need for this school's families, and it usually is not about grammar. It is about structuring a commentary or essay so an examiner can follow the argument without having to work for it, using topic sentences that actually signal what is coming, and using evidence precisely rather than generally. A tutor working on this should be reviewing the student's actual recent written work, not running generic essay-writing exercises unrelated to the DP assessment criteria.

Physics and Chemistry requests tend to concentrate around HL depth and Paper 3 data-based questions, while Math AA HL and AI HL requests split between ongoing content support and focused exam-technique work closer to May or November. A tutor who treats every subject the same way, without adjusting for these different underlying needs, is not really matching what Bangalore families are actually asking for.

Availability is always conditional; a specific specialist for, say, Economics essay technique, can be reviewed subject to current schedule, not guaranteed instantly on request.

Tutoring in that compressed window can improve technique on the highest-yield areas, but it works better, and produces more durable results, the earlier it starts. faqs.question: My child's predicted grade is a 6 in Economics — can tutoring realistically push it to a 7?
faqs.answer: It depends on why the gap exists. If the issue is essay technique, answers describing rather than evaluating against the command term, that is genuinely fixable with focused practice over a few months, and a 6 becoming a 7 is a realistic goal to work toward, though never guaranteed. If the gap reflects weaker underlying content knowledge, the timeline needed is longer. A tutor should diagnose which situation applies before promising anything about the outcome.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring reliable enough for DP subjects, or is a home tutor always better for North Bangalore families?
faqs.answer: Neither is universally better. Online tutoring often gives access to a stronger subject specialist than what is locally available, which matters more for DP-level Physics or Math AA HL than for general homework support. Home tutoring suits younger students or families wanting an in-person presence for organisation and accountability. Many North Bangalore families connected to this school end up using a hybrid mix: online for subject depth, occasional home sessions for writing structure or planning.

faqs.question: What if the tutor doesn't turn out to be the right fit for my child?
faqs.answer: Raise it directly rather than persisting through a full term hoping it improves. A mismatch, in teaching style or in actual subject depth, is treated as something to resolve, not a complaint to argue about, and a different tutor can be reviewed subject to availability for that subject and level. Genuine DP-level specialists in a specific subject combination are a narrower pool than general tutors, so a replacement may take a little longer, but persisting rarely helps.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help specifically with English writing structure, not just grammar correction?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the more common specific requests connected to this school. A tutor working on writing structure reviews the student's actual recent essays or commentaries and focuses on how an argument is built, topic sentences, evidence use, and directly answering the command term, rather than correcting surface grammar. This kind of support applies beyond English A too, since Economics, TOK and IA writing all reward the same underlying structural clarity.

faqs.question: Can tutoring help with the Extended Essay or Internal Assessments?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to tutor availability for the relevant subject area. Support typically means helping refine the student's own research question or exploration topic and reviewing drafts against IB's specific assessment criteria, not writing or substantially rewriting content for the student, which would breach academic honesty requirements. A tutor who treats the early topic-selection stage seriously, not just the final draft review, tends to produce a stronger, more genuinely the student's own piece of work.

faqs.question: How do you match a tutor if we are open to either North Bangalore or online?
faqs.answer: Say so directly when reaching out, since it widens the realistic pool of tutors considerably. IB Gram will consider tutors based in North Bangalore, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road or Indiranagar for home sessions, alongside online specialists from anywhere with strong DP-subject depth, and suggest whichever combination best matches the subject, level and family schedule. Being flexible on mode, especially for a harder-to-find subject combination, often means faster and better matching overall.

faqs.question: We're only a few months from the May 2026 exam session — is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the plan should look different from one starting a year out. A tutor at this stage typically prioritises the highest-yield gaps, common technical errors, weak topics likely to appear, and timed practice under real exam conditions, rather than a full syllabus re-teach. This can meaningfully improve exam-day performance and close some of the predicted-to-final gap, though it cannot fully substitute for consistent practice not done earlier in the year.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram cover younger students at this school, not just DP-level ones?
faqs.answer: Yes. IB Gram reviews requests spanning Grade 1 through Grade 12, including Primary Years Programme and Middle Years Programme support for younger Canadian International School Bangalore students, not only DP-level tutoring. Building strong criterion-literacy and independent writing habits during MYP tends to reduce how much remedial work is needed once a student reaches Grade 11, so earlier requests, even without an urgent deadline, are reviewed just as seriously as exam-season DP ones.

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing Two Tutor Profiles the Right Way
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents comparing tutors for a child at Indus International School Bangalore end up looking at the wrong things first, years of experience, a confident phone manner, a recommendation from another parent, none of which reliably predicts whether a specific tutor will help with a specific gap. A more useful comparison starts with three concrete questions: has this tutor actually taught the exact subject and level needed, HL or SL, MYP or DP; can they describe, in their own words, what a criterion-related assessment actually rewards at this grade; and what would their first session look like for this particular student, not a generic first lesson.

Two tutors who look similar on paper, similar experience, similar subject list, can differ enormously once tested against these three questions. One might describe a first session as diagnostic, working from the student's last assessed piece; the other might describe it as an introduction to their teaching style, with no reference to the student's actual current work. The first answer is a far better signal. introSummary: Families searching for IB tutors in Stonehill International School Bangalore usually fall into one of two moments: the start of the year, when the goal is settling into a subject's pace and expectations, or the stretch toward March, when mocks and IAs compress everything into a shorter window. contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Changes Between August and March at Stonehill
contentBlocks.body: August looks different from March for almost every DP student at an international school like Stonehill, and a tutoring plan that ignores that arc tends to waste the family's money on the wrong kind of help at the wrong time. In August, the actual need is usually settling: understanding a new HL subject's pace, closing summer gaps in Math or a science before the syllabus accelerates, and building a working rhythm around Stonehill's own timetable and homework load. By November, the picture shifts toward IA topics and EE research questions, since most schools expect meaningful drafts well before the calendar year ends. By January and February, mocks dominate, and the useful work is timed-paper practice and command-term precision rather than new content. By March, for a May-session student, the job is narrower still: targeted revision on the specific topics a mock actually exposed, not a broad re-teach of the whole syllabus. A family calling IB Gram in August is usually solving a different problem than a family calling in February, even if both say the same thing, 'we need an IB tutor,' and treating both requests identically wastes the early months when the most durable gains are actually possible. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with Stonehill International School; what follows reflects general North Bangalore DP patterns, not insider knowledge of the school's own curriculum delivery.

contentBlocks.heading: DP Math and Sciences: What Stonehill Families Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body: DP Math, in both AA HL and AI HL, is the single most requested subject for families connected to Stonehill, which fits a broader North Bangalore pattern of ambitious students aiming at engineering, economics or data-focused university courses. AA HL suits students who are comfortable with proof and abstract calculus; AI HL suits students who prefer applied, modelling-based problems, and the two are not interchangeable, a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. Physics and Chemistry, at HL or SL depending on the student's course combination, come up frequently around IA data-analysis stage, when a student has results but cannot structure the write-up against the assessment criteria examiners actually reward. Economics tutoring tends to focus on IA commentary specifically, since students often understand a concept correctly but struggle to connect it to a real, dated article the way the assessment format demands. English A support is usually less about grammar and more about building a defensible written argument under time pressure in commentary and essay tasks. None of these subjects gets taught in isolation from the wider DP structure; a tutor working on an Economics IA will still reference TOK-style evaluation, and a Math tutor will still touch on how a Paper 3 investigation reads for an examiner. IB Gram matches for the specific subject, level and current stage a Stonehill family actually needs.

contentBlocks.body: IB Gram works with students from Grade 1 to Grade 12 in the North Bangalore corridor, spanning the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. Most enquiries connected to Stonehill are DP-focused, given how demanding the last two years become, but younger siblings often need something entirely different: PYP-age children typically need gentle reading, numeracy and unit-of-inquiry support rather than exam coaching, while MYP-age students usually need help turning open-ended classroom tasks into work that actually meets the specific assessment criteria a subject is graded against. Treating all three as the same kind of 'IB tutoring' misses how different the actual skill is at each stage. A DP tutor skilled at HL Maths timed-paper technique is often the wrong fit for a Grade 5 sibling who needs patience and encouragement, and a gentle primary-years tutor rarely has the depth for a Paper 3 investigation three months before a May session. IB Gram matches by programme level first, before subject or mode, specifically to avoid this kind of mismatch. For families with children at more than one stage, which is common, coordinating tutors across PYP, MYP and DP as one ongoing relationship tends to work better than restarting the search separately each time a child moves up a level.

contentBlocks.heading: The Gap Between a Predicted Grade and a Final One
contentBlocks.body:
A school's predicted grade for a Diploma Programme student is an informed estimate — based on classwork, mock results and a teacher's read of trajectory — not a guarantee of what May 2026 or November 2026 exam boards will award. For families connected to American Embassy School in Chanakyapuri, that gap matters because the school's own timetable, extracurricular calendar and international mobility (families relocating mid-cycle, students joining after Grade 10 elsewhere) can leave holes that a predicted grade doesn't capture. A student predicted a 6 in Math AA HL on classroom performance alone can still land a 4 if paper technique, timed practice or IA structure were never actually tested under exam conditions.

IB Gram exists to close that specific gap, not to replace what the school already does well. Tutoring here spans Grade 1 to Grade 12, so support can start as early as consolidating PYP foundations or as late as a focused eight-week push before November mocks. For a Diploma student, the work usually means past-paper practice under time pressure, structured IA and EE feedback, and TOK essay planning that a busy school timetable often can't fit in. None of this replaces the school's own teaching; it sits alongside it, aimed at the specific place where a predicted grade and a final one tend to diverge.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Tutor Actually Covers for Diploma Subjects Here
contentBlocks.body:
The subjects families ask about most for students connected to American Embassy School are Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A — the core cluster that tends to decide a Diploma Programme average one way or the other. Math is usually the first call: a student who chose AA HL for university requirements but is struggling with proof-based algebra or calculus needs a tutor who can rebuild technique without slowing the whole syllabus down, while an AI HL student often needs more work on modelling and real-world application questions that Paper 3 leans on heavily.

Physics and Chemistry tutoring tends to split into two needs: closing content gaps before a topic test, and building the analytical writing a good Internal Assessment demands — a lab report that states a hypothesis clearly, controls variables honestly and discusses uncertainty instead of ignoring it. Economics support is different again; most requests are about essay structure for Paper 1 and 2, and about turning a student's economic intuition into the vocabulary examiners are trained to reward. English A tutoring usually starts with close reading and moves to comparative essay technique for Paper 2, since that is where marks are lost even by strong readers who write well in isolation but struggle to compare two unseen texts under time pressure. Subject depth matters more than general tutoring credentials for every one of these.
items: Math AA HL and Math AI HL — technique, modelling, Paper 3
Physics and Chemistry — content gaps plus IA lab-report writing
Economics — Paper 1/2 essay structure and terminology
English A — comparative essay technique for Paper 2
HL/SL mismatches reviewed before committing to a long-term plan

contentBlocks.heading: How Support Differs Across PYP, MYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years Programme tutoring, for ages roughly 3 to 12, rarely looks like formal instruction. It is usually a parent noticing a child has fallen behind on reading fluency or number sense and wanting a patient adult to work through it twice a week, in a way that does not feel like extra school. Middle Years Programme tutoring, covering ages 11 to 16, is where subject-specific gaps start to matter — a student weak in algebra before Grade 9 will carry that weakness into Diploma-level Math AA or AI unless it is addressed directly, and MYP personal project support is a common, specific ask in the months before submission.

Diploma Programme tutoring, for ages 16 to 19, is the densest of the three because it carries the most external assessment weight: Extended Essay mentoring across a full academic year, Theory of Knowledge essay planning against the prescribed titles, Internal Assessments across multiple subjects with their own deadlines, and exam preparation for May or November sessions. A family that starts Diploma-level tutoring in Grade 11 has more room to build genuine subject depth than one that starts in the final term before exams, when the realistic goal shifts from mastery to damage control on the weakest two or three topics. Being honest about which of those two situations a family is actually in changes what a tutor should spend the first month doing.
items: PYP (ages 3-12): reading, number sense, foundational habits
MYP (ages 11-16): subject gaps, personal project support
DP (ages 16-19): IA, EE, TOK, Paper 1/2/3 preparation
Earlier start in Grade 11 allows depth; late start means triage

Delhi families connected to American Embassy School generally choose between three formats: home tutoring, online tutoring, or a hybrid of both. Home tutoring can work for families in or near Chanakyapuri and nearby South Delhi pockets — Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket — where a tutor can realistically reach on a consistent weekly schedule without traffic turning a one-hour session into a three-hour commitment. Online tutoring is available across Delhi for every supported IB programme and subject, and it is often the better choice for two specific reasons: a family wants a subject specialist who happens to live across town, or the family's own schedule — travel, activities, a student splitting time between two homes after a relocation — makes a fixed home slot unrealistic.

The honest trade-off is this: home tutoring builds a working relationship faster for younger students who need patient hand-holding, but it caps how far a family can search for the right subject expert. Online tutoring removes that geographic limit but asks more of the student in terms of self-discipline during the session. Many families land on hybrid support — home sessions for a core subject like Math, online sessions for a specialist need like Economics essay coaching — because it lets them optimise for both proximity and expertise instead of picking one over the other.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really understand this school's specific expectations?
faqs.answer: A tutor's value here comes from IB curriculum familiarity and current assessment-criteria knowledge, not from formal affiliation with any particular school — IB Gram has no official connection with American Embassy School or any other school named on this page. What can be checked and matched is a tutor's experience with the relevant Diploma, Middle Years or Primary Years subject, their track record with similar-aged students, and their comfort with the assessment format the student will actually sit. faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor isn't a good fit?
faqs.answer: This comes up more than families expect, and it is treated as a normal part of matching rather than a failure. If a trial or early session shows the personality fit or teaching style isn't right — even when the subject knowledge is strong — a second match is arranged instead of asking the student to push through it. Raising the concern early, ideally within the first two or three sessions, makes the switch smoother and avoids losing weeks of momentum right before a mock exam or an IA deadline.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work as well as home tutoring?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma subjects, yes, provided the student can concentrate through a screen and has a quiet space during the session — the syllabus, the past papers and the IA feedback process are identical either way. Where online genuinely struggles is with younger children who need more physical presence to stay engaged, or with subjects that involve a lot of handwritten working a tutor needs to see closely. For a family near American Embassy School choosing between a nearby generalist and a stronger online specialist, the specialist is usually the better trade for Diploma-level work.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic if we live in Vasant Vihar or Greater Kailash?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, for a consistent weekly slot — these are among the South Delhi pockets where home tutoring is workable for students connected to American Embassy School. The harder scenario is an irregular schedule that shifts week to week, since Delhi traffic makes last-minute rescheduling difficult for a tutor covering multiple families across the city. A fixed slot, ideally avoiding the worst of evening peak traffic, works far better than an ad-hoc arrangement. If timing keeps slipping, switching that particular subject to an online slot is usually the more reliable fix.

faqs.question: How is Extended Essay mentoring different from regular subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: EE mentoring runs across most of an academic year rather than in weekly subject lessons, and it focuses on research question refinement, structuring an argument across roughly 4,000 words, and meeting the school's own internal deadlines for drafts. A good EE mentor pushes back on a topic that is too broad or not researchable within the time available, rather than simply cheering on whatever idea a student first proposes. It sits alongside subject tutoring rather than replacing it — a student can be getting Chemistry tutoring and EE mentoring from two different tutors at once.

faqs.question: What if my child is just starting Grade 11 and hasn't struggled yet?
faqs.answer: Starting early, before a specific problem shows up, is the situation with the most options — a tutor can help build strong IA habits, exam technique and time-management from the outset rather than fixing gaps under pressure later. It is a smaller, lighter engagement than crisis tutoring before mocks, often just fortnightly check-ins on a subject like Math AA or Physics rather than intensive weekly sessions. Families sometimes feel it is premature to start this early; in practice, it is usually the cheapest and least stressful point to begin, precisely because nothing has gone wrong yet.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, if a tutor's background genuinely spans both subjects at the right level — Math and Physics is a common pairing, for instance — but IB Gram generally avoids stretching a single tutor across unrelated subjects like Economics and Chemistry just for convenience. Subject depth tends to suffer when a tutor is covering too broad a range, particularly at HL. Most families end up with one tutor per subject, coordinated loosely around a shared weekly schedule, rather than one generalist trying to cover everything.

faqs.question: How soon before May or November exams should tutoring start?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on where the student currently stands. A student already close to their target grade can often get real value from a focused six-to-eight-week push covering past papers and weak topics before May 2026 or November 2026 sessions. A student with genuine content gaps across a subject needs considerably longer — starting the term before, not the month before — because there simply isn't time to both learn new content and build exam technique in a few weeks. Being honest about which situation applies matters more than the calendar date itself.

faqs.question: Do you offer trial sessions before committing?
faqs.answer: Yes — most families have an introductory or trial session with a proposed tutor before agreeing to a term-long plan, specifically to check subject clarity and personality fit before any commitment is made. This isn't a sales session; it should feel like an actual diagnostic, with the tutor asking about recent test results, current weak spots and what the student has already tried. If it doesn't feel right, saying so before the first proper session begins costs nothing and saves both sides time later.

contentBlocks.heading: How to Actually Compare Two IB Tutors Before You Pick One
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents shortlisting IB tutors in DPS International Saket Delhi make the comparison on the wrong axis — years of experience, or a friend's recommendation, rather than fit for the actual subject and level. A tutor who is excellent at DP Math AA HL may never have taught MYP writing, and the two skills do not transfer automatically. Before you commit to anyone, ask three specific questions on the first call: which grade bands they have taught inside the last two years, whether they have handled IA planning or EE mentoring recently, and how they structure a first session with a student they have never met.

Saket sits close to a cluster of international and CBSE-plus schools, and IB Gram sees requests across Grade 1 to Grade 12 — from a Primary Years Programme parent who wants reading support, to a DP student six weeks from May 2026 mocks who needs Physics HL revision under time pressure. These are not the same tutoring problem, and a tutor good at one is not automatically good at the other.

A proper comparison also checks logistics honestly. Can the tutor actually reach a South Delhi home twice a week without the commute eating the session, or is online tutoring the more reliable option here? IB Gram's matching process is built around answering that before the first trial session, not after a term has been lost figuring it out.

contentBlocks.heading: What PYP, MYP and DP Actually Require From a Tutor Near Saket
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme, running roughly from age 3 to 12, asks for something different from a tutor than the Diploma Programme does. A PYP parent near DPS International Saket is usually looking for someone who can build reading stamina and number sense through inquiry-based tasks, not drill worksheets — the programme resists rote repetition by design, so a tutor who only knows how to explain formulas struggles here.

Middle Years Programme families, covering ages 11 to 16, are the ones most often searching for MYP writing support specifically. The personal project and subject-specific criteria reward structured argument and reflection, and a student who writes fluently in English can still lose marks for not addressing the criteria directly. A tutor who has actually reviewed MYP work against those criteria is worth more here than one who simply knows the subject content.

Diploma Programme students, ages 16 to 19, carry the heaviest and most varied load: Math AA or AI at HL or SL, Physics or Chemistry at HL or SL, Economics essays, English A close reading, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge running alongside regular coursework. DP Math and Science revision are the two most common requests IB Gram receives from Saket and South Delhi families, particularly in the months before May and November exam sessions, when past-paper practice matters more than new content.

What can be stated honestly is the process: subject-matter background is checked, familiarity with IB assessment objectives is confirmed, and recent teaching experience at the requested grade band is verified before a tutor is suggested for a match.

It is also fair to ask what happens if the match does not work. A rigid multi-month contract with no exit is a red flag in this business; a family should be able to review the arrangement after a defined trial period without penalty. IB Gram structures its matching this way deliberately — continuation is always subject to tutor availability and an honest check-in on progress, not locked in from day one.

faqs.question: My child is starting IB at Grade 9 with no prior exposure — is it too late to catch up?
faqs.answer: No, Grade 9 is early rather than late for MYP, and there is real time to build the foundation properly before DP begins in Grade 11. The situation is different for a student starting serious support only in Grade 11 with DP already underway — options narrow considerably there, and the honest goal shifts from mastering everything to prioritising the highest-impact topics before mocks. Starting now, at Grade 9, still allows a tutor to build genuine understanding rather than exam shortcuts, which matters more for how DP goes later.

faqs.question: Should my child do Math AA or Math AI for DP?
faqs.answer: This depends on university plans and comfort with abstract proof-based math, not on which is considered more prestigious. Math AA suits students likely to study engineering, physical sciences or economics-heavy degrees that expect calculus fluency; Math AI suits students who reason well with applied, real-world problems but find pure proof-based work draining. A tutor can genuinely help assess this around mid-Grade 11 by working through sample problems from both syllabuses with the student, rather than the family guessing based on reputation alone. Switching tracks later than this becomes progressively harder to justify.

contentBlocks.heading: What Changes at The British School New Delhi Between August and May
contentBlocks.body:
Walk into a Diploma Programme classroom near Chanakyapuri in August and the room is still finding its shape. Subject groups have just settled, students are weighing Math AA against Math AI, and the Extended Essay is a vague idea rather than a topic. By May, the same student is sitting a timed Paper 2 with a research question they defended months earlier. What happens in between is where most of the actual learning, and most of the actual stress, sits.

For a family connected to The British School New Delhi, the shift usually starts around the first internal deadlines in October and November, when real gaps in Physics HL, Economics essay technique or English A commentary writing become visible for the first time. IB tutors in The British School New Delhi, Delhi are typically brought in at one of three points: early, to build subject confidence before it is tested; mid-year, once a mock paper or teacher comment has flagged a specific weakness; or late, when May is close and the work is mostly exam technique and past-paper timing. None of these entry points is wrong. But starting in January to fix a gap that has existed since September is harder than starting in October, and it helps to say that plainly rather than promise a quick fix.

By April, study leave changes the rhythm again: less new content, more structured revision, more attention to command terms and mark schemes.

Some families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad also look for tutors who understand Delhi's IB tutoring market even though they sit, strictly speaking, in NCR rather than Delhi proper.

None of this changes the subject content. It changes whether IB home tuition near The British School New Delhi in Delhi is realistic to ask for, or whether the session should simply happen online.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Diploma Programme Students Actually Get Stuck
contentBlocks.body:
Families looking for an IB Maths tutor or IB Science tutor near The British School New Delhi tend to ask for help in a fairly narrow band: Math AA HL or Math AI HL when a student is deciding which is realistic, Physics and Chemistry when HL content moves faster than school pace, Economics when essay structure and evaluation are weaker than the content knowledge, and English A when literary commentary needs more than general writing skill.

Math is usually the subject where the AA-versus-AI decision itself needs input, not just tutoring after the choice is made. A student comfortable with algebraic manipulation but slow under time pressure often does better with a tutor who drills timed Paper 1 questions rather than reteaching content already known. Physics HL and Chemistry HL, at this school as at most IB schools, are where students lose marks on command terms and multi-step calculations rather than on core concepts, and a tutor who focuses only on content misses that.

English A and humanities writing come up constantly, and not always from students who are academically weak elsewhere. A strong Math AA student can still write a flat Paper 1 commentary because literary analysis is a different skill entirely. IA planning threads through every subject: a Math IA that starts as 'something about statistics' needs a narrower, markable research question well before the deadline feels close.

contentBlocks.heading: From Primary Years to the Diploma: What Support Looks Like at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body:
Support spans Grade 1 to Grade 12, which in IB terms means the Primary Years Programme (roughly ages 3 to 12), the Middle Years Programme (ages 11 to 16) and the Diploma Programme (ages 16 to 19). Each stage needs a different kind of help, and treating them the same is a common mistake.

PYP tutoring is mostly about building reading, writing and number confidence alongside the inquiry-based units the school runs; it rarely means formal exam prep. MYP tutoring starts to look more like subject support, criteria-based assessment (the familiar A, B, C, D bands) and the beginnings of structured assignment planning, including groundwork for the eventual Personal Project. Diploma Programme tutoring is where most demand concentrates, because it carries the heaviest external assessment load: six subject groups, TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS running in parallel, with Paper 1, 2 and sometimes 3 exams at the end.

A Grade 7 student and a Grade 12 student asking for 'IB tutoring' are, in practice, asking for almost unrelated things. The programme stage should shape the request from the start, not get discovered halfway through the first session.

contentBlocks.heading: Being Honest About What Tutoring Can and Cannot Fix
contentBlocks.body:
It would be easy to promise that the right tutor guarantees a particular grade. That promise would also be false, and IB Gram does not make it. Outcomes depend on the student's starting point, how consistently sessions actually happen, what the school itself is covering, and factors no tutor controls, like how a specific exam paper is set that year.

What tutoring can reasonably do is narrower and more useful: close a specific, identified gap; turn a vague IA idea into a research question that can actually be marked; turn unstructured revision into a plan with a schedule attached to it. Families who come in expecting a specific number, a 6 turning into a 7 by a fixed date, are usually disappointed even when the tutoring itself is good, because that framing was never realistic to begin with.

One honest limitation worth stating plainly: a tutor who lives an hour from Chanakyapuri in evening traffic is not a good home-tutoring match, however strong their subject knowledge, and pretending otherwise wastes everyone's time. Online is often the better answer in that exact situation, not a compromise.

Availability, at any point, depends on level, subject and schedule, and should be treated as something to check rather than something to assume.

contentBlocks.heading: The Assumption That Costs DP1 Students a Term at Lancers International School
contentBlocks.body:
The most common wrong assumption sounds entirely reasonable. The IB is a continuous assessment programme, the school is a strong one, so a student who keeps up in class will not need help from outside.

It holds until DP1. Then the internal assessments start, and continuous assessment turns out to mean several long independent projects running in parallel, each marked against criteria the student has never used before, with a supervisor who can advise but cannot draft. A student who has always kept up in class has no practice at all with unsupervised long-form work. That is the gap that opens in the second term, and it opens quickly.

The second version of the assumption is quieter. Parents believe that if something were going wrong, the school would say so. Schools do say so, but they say it on the reporting cycle, which can be six or eight weeks after the problem began.

None of this is a criticism of the school. Every IB school runs the same model, and it is the model rather than the teaching that produces the gap.

IB tutors in Lancers International School Gurugram are asked for most often in exactly this window: DP1, second term, first internal assessment, no clear idea where to begin. That timing is predictable, which means it can be planned for instead of reacted to.

Supervisors advise, they do not draft
Reports arrive six to eight weeks after the problem
DP1 second term is the usual pressure point

contentBlocks.heading: Golf Course Road Logistics: Getting a Tutor to Sector 53 and DLF Phase 5
contentBlocks.body:
The school sits on Golf Course Road, and so do most of the families using this page. That makes the travel question easier here than in almost any other part of Gurugram.

Sector 53 and Sector 54 are the simplest, with the Rapid Metro corridor running alongside and tutors able to take two sessions in one evening without a long transfer between them. DLF Phase 5, around The Crest and DLF Park Place, is effectively the same catchment. Sushant Lok and Sector 57, sitting behind Sushant Lok 3 on Golf Course Extension Road, add ten or fifteen minutes and remain workable through the week.

The harder runs are Sohna Road, past Vatika Chowk towards Sector 49 and Sector 50, and the newer stretches around Sector 65 and Nirvana Country. They are fine in the afternoon and slow at exactly the hour DP students become free. South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 sit somewhere in between.

Distance is not the useful measure on this road. Direction of travel is. A tutor coming inward from the Sohna Road side at 6 30 pm has a very different evening from one coming down from Sector 53, and that difference decides whether a slot survives past November.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Online Slots and the Hybrid Middle for Lancers International School Families
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring along this stretch of Golf Course Road is more practical than in most parts of the city, so families here often start with it and stay. It suits PYP and MYP students, who work better with someone at the same table, and it suits parents who want to hear how a session is going without having to ask.

Online earns its place in three situations. Rare higher level combinations, where the right specialist may be in Delhi or Noida rather than two sectors away. Late slots, after a match or a rehearsal, when nobody wants a tutor arriving at 9 pm. And the fortnight before mocks, when three short sessions beat one long one and travel time becomes the binding constraint.

Hybrid handles the rest. A weekly home session for teaching, an online midweek slot for doubt-solving and draft review, and additional online time added only when a deadline demands it.

There is a real cost to online with younger children, and it deserves saying plainly. A Grade 4 child alone with a laptop drifts. Either an adult stays in the room for the first few weeks or the session is better held at home. Availability for any of these arrangements depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed once the slot you need is clear.

contentBlocks.heading: Sciences and Mathematics: The Two Requests That Come Up Most
contentBlocks.body:
Physics, Chemistry and the two mathematics courses account for most of what families connected to this school ask about, which matches the higher level choices that tend to run here.

Physics at higher level goes wrong in a specific place. Students handle the mechanics and then struggle when a paper asks them to justify rather than calculate, and the internal assessment punishes a research question chosen because the equipment was available rather than because the relationship was worth investigating. Fixing that after data collection is not possible, which is why the first session on a Physics IA should happen before the method is finalised.

Chemistry follows a similar shape, with organic mechanisms, equilibrium and the treatment of uncertainty as the recurring requests.

Math AA at higher level is the heaviest single ask. The gap is almost always algebraic fluency rather than the current topic, and closing it takes weeks of short daily work rather than one long weekly session. Math AI at higher level trips students on the statistics papers and on modelling questions where choosing the right tool is the actual difficulty.

Economics and English A come up less often and later, usually around the first commentary and the individual oral. Both benefit from an early start more than students expect them to.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Shortlists a Tutor for a Lancers International School Student
contentBlocks.body:
The brief that produces a good match is short but specific: grade, programme, subject and level, the deadline that is closest, the residential sector, and the two evenings that are genuinely free once school and activities are accounted for.

What happens next is a narrowing rather than a search. Tutors are considered for the level rather than the subject name, since Physics at higher level and Physics at standard level attract different people. The school calendar is taken into account, because a student with an internal assessment due in three weeks needs a different tutor from one starting a two-year plan. Mode is decided before any name is shared, so that a strong online option is not lost to an assumption that home must be better.

Two or three profiles follow, with the reasoning written down, and a first session that is meant to be tested rather than accepted.

What is deliberately not promised is a named tutor by a fixed date. Availability depends on level and schedule, and the late evening slots that suit DP students fill first each term. contentBlocks.heading: PYP Inquiry, MYP Foundations, DP Load: Support That Changes Shape
contentBlocks.body:
The tutor's actual job changes name three times across the school years, even when the person stays the same.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages 3 to 12, the tutor is closer to a reading and thinking companion. The measurable work is fluency, number confidence and vocabulary. The unmeasurable work is keeping a child willing to ask about something they do not understand. Heavy worksheet drilling at this stage buys a short-term result and costs the thing the programme is built on.

In the Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, the tutor becomes a translator. Criterion strands, command terms, investigation structure and reflection are the vocabulary of every assignment, and a student who can decode them plans better and rewrites less. MYP foundations are also where the mathematics and science habits that DP quietly assumes are either built or missed.

In the Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, the tutor is a project manager with subject expertise. Six subjects, three at higher level, plus TOK, CAS and the Extended Essay, on submission dates that do not negotiate.

Families with children at two of these stages usually need two tutors. Better to hear that at the enquiry stage than to discover it in week three.

contentBlocks.heading: Documents, Demo and the Independence Check
contentBlocks.body:
Screening runs in three gates, and a tutor who clears all three still has to pass the trial session with your child.

The first gate is documentary. Identity and qualifications are collected and checked against the profile that will be shown to you. Claims about examining or moderation work are verified rather than repeated, because that particular claim is the easiest one to make and the most persuasive to a worried parent.

The second gate is a subject demonstration. A past paper answer, a markscheme, and a conversation about why the answer scored what it did. Teaching ability shows up faster here than in any curriculum vitae. A tutor who can explain the difference between a four-mark and a six-mark response understands the assessment model. One who only knows the content does not.

The third gate is independence. Tutors are told plainly that they do not speak for any school, cannot claim inside knowledge of a school's marking, and must not describe themselves as connected to one. A tutor who leans on a school name to win a family has failed this gate outright.

After that, parent feedback in the first month decides whether the tutor stays in rotation. Repeated lateness or vague session summaries end it.

contentBlocks.heading: Honest Limits: What Tutoring Near Golf Course Road Cannot Fix
contentBlocks.body:
Some things a tutor can move quickly. Others cannot be bought at any hourly rate, and knowing the difference saves a term.

A tutor can fix technique, and reasonably fast. Command terms, answer structure, time allocation across Paper 1, the shape of an internal assessment. Those often show up within three or four weeks.

A tutor cannot manufacture time. A student carrying three co-curricular commitments and a competitive sport has no room for two extra sessions a week, and adding them produces missed homework rather than progress. A tutor also cannot repair a subject choice made against the student's grain. Where a student is in the wrong mathematics course, the honest advice is a conversation with the school, not more hours at the desk.

Starting late has real limits too. Six weeks before a final paper, the plan is triage: protect the topics carrying the highest mark weight, drill technique, accept that some content will not be covered. That is a legitimate plan and worth doing. It is simply not the same plan as starting in DP1.

No one can guarantee a grade in an externally assessed programme, and a tutor promising one has told you what to expect from the rest of their advice.

contentBlocks.body:
Four details make the shortlist useful: the grade and programme, the subject with its level, the closest deadline, and the sector you live in. If there has been an earlier tutor, one line on what did not work is worth more than a paragraph on what you want.

IB Gram then reviews the request against tutors currently taking students around Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok and Sector 57, and weighs home, online and hybrid rather than defaulting to one of them. faqs.question: Do you provide tutors specifically for students at Lancers International School?
faqs.answer: Tutors are matched to a student's subject, level and timetable, and many already work with students attending schools along Golf Course Road. That familiarity helps with practical things: when reports go out, when internal assessment drafts are collected, how much notice students get before mocks. It does not mean anything more than that. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with the school, and no tutor has access to school marking or internal feedback. If a tutor claims otherwise, treat it as a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: When in DP1 is the right time to start Physics or Chemistry support?
faqs.answer: Before the internal assessment method is finalised, which in most schools means the first or second term of DP1. The research question and the variable design carry a large share of the marks and cannot be improved once data collection is done. Content support can begin at any point, but the assessment work has a real cutoff. For a student who is simply finding higher level content heavy, starting in the first term is far easier than waiting for a poor test result to make the argument for you.

faqs.question: Is help with an internal assessment allowed, or does it break academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Guidance is allowed and expected; drafting is not. A tutor can teach the criteria, question a weak research question, discuss method design, explain how uncertainty should be treated, and give feedback on writing the student has produced. A tutor cannot write sections, rewrite paragraphs into their own phrasing, or supply analysis to be copied down. The test the supervisor will apply is whether the student can explain every line unprompted. Any tutor unwilling to hold that boundary is a risk to the diploma rather than an asset.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP into DP next year. What is worth doing over the summer?
faqs.answer: Two things, and neither is exam practice. The first is mathematics fluency, since most DP difficulty in the sciences traces back to algebra that never became automatic. Twenty minutes daily beats a long weekly session for this. The second is reading and writing volume in the subject they will take for English A or their humanities choice, because DP essays assume a reading speed that MYP does not build on its own. A short summer plan is usually four to six sessions, not twenty.

faqs.question: Can home sessions work if we live in Sector 65 or off Sohna Road?
faqs.answer: They can, with a realistic slot. Both are comfortable in the afternoon and considerably slower between 6 and 8 pm, which is when most DP students finally become free. Families in those areas often keep weekday sessions online and book home visits for weekend mornings, which holds up much better across a full term than an optimistic weekday arrangement that starts slipping by November. Availability for a home slot depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed once you tell us the sector and the hour you need.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP higher level subject usually need?
faqs.answer: Two is the common answer during term, with one longer teaching session and one shorter review, though a student who is broadly fine and only wants doubt-solving may need one. The number rises around an internal assessment deadline or in the weeks before mocks, then falls back. What matters more than frequency is whether the work set between sessions actually gets done. Three sessions a week booked into a timetable with room for two produces cancellations, and cancellations are usually how an arrangement quietly ends.

faqs.question: What should the first session look like so we know it went well?
faqs.answer: It should be mostly diagnostic. The tutor should look at recent work, ask the student to attempt something while explaining their thinking, and finish with a plan for the next few weeks that names specific topics or assessment components. A session that is pure teaching from the first minute is a warning sign, because the tutor has decided what is wrong before checking. Afterwards, ask the student whether the tutor explained things or simply solved them. That answer is the most reliable early signal you will get.

faqs.question: Are fees higher for tutors familiar with this school and area?
faqs.answer: Fees track programme, level and mode rather than school familiarity. Higher level DP subjects sit above standard level, and the sciences and mathematics above the humanities, because the specialist pool is smaller. Home sessions carry a practical travel premium, since a tutor crossing the city at 7 pm gives up a second slot, which is why online is usually cheaper for the same person. Indicative ranges for your specific subject and level are shared once the request is understood, before any tutor is introduced.

faqs.question: We want support for a Grade 3 child and a DP2 student. Can that be arranged together?
faqs.answer: It can be arranged, but almost certainly with two different tutors. The Grade 3 work is reading confidence, number sense and keeping curiosity intact, and it needs someone who genuinely enjoys that age. The DP2 work is subject specialism and deadline management under real pressure. Very few people are good at both, and a compromise choice usually shortchanges the younger child. Scheduling the two on the same evening at the same address is often possible and worth asking for directly.

contentBlocks.heading: The gap between a predicted grade and a final grade at Pathways World School
contentBlocks.body:
A predicted grade is a professional estimate, prepared by teachers and sent to universities during the autumn of the second Diploma Programme year. The final grade arrives the following July. When those two numbers differ by two or three points, ability is rarely the cause. The cause is usually a small set of repeated, fixable habits: a Paper 2 answer that describes when the command term asked the student to evaluate, working that skips the one line an examiner needs before awarding method marks, or an internal assessment built on a research question too broad to reach the top band.

Tutoring that closes that gap has to be diagnostic before it is instructional. The first job is to read the actual evidence, which means mock scripts, marked assignments and teacher comments, and to find the pattern inside them. Content revision only makes sense afterwards.

Families connected with Pathways World School tend to arrive with exactly this brief. They want Diploma Programme subject depth, clearer Middle Years assignment structure, and a weekly plan that survives a long school day and an activity-heavy calendar. Some ask from Grade 6 onwards so that the Diploma does not land as a shock two years later.

One point of clarity before anything else: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with Pathways World School, or with any other school named on this page.
items: Mock scripts read before any lesson plan is written
Command-term errors separated from genuine content gaps
IA research questions narrowed to something markable
Grade 1 to Grade 12, not only the two Diploma years
An independent platform, with no school affiliation

contentBlocks.heading: How a shortlist gets built for a Pathways World School student in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Matching runs in four steps, and none of them involve handing you a directory to browse on your own.

Step one is an intake conversation. Programme, year group, subjects and levels, the assessment calendar for the term, session preference, and the window in the week when the student can actually concentrate rather than the window that merely exists on a timetable. Parents often name Tuesday evening; the honest answer is frequently Saturday morning.

Step two is filtering. Tutors are filtered by the level they have taught, not by the subject word. Math AA HL and Math AI HL are separate jobs with separate examiner expectations, and someone fluent in one is not automatically the right person for the other.

Step three is a short list, usually two or three profiles. Each comes with what the tutor has taught, how a session is structured, and their current availability, which is subject to tutor schedules rather than fixed in advance.

Step four is a trial session, and your job during it is to watch. Does the tutor ask the student to explain their reasoning before correcting it. Is work set with a deadline attached. Can the tutor say what the next four sessions will cover.

If the trial does not land, say so quickly. Changing tutor after one session costs a week. A poor fit left running for a term costs considerably more than that.

Filtering by level taught, not by subject name
Two or three profiles, with structure and availability stated

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and Diploma support from Grade 1 through Grade 12
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes ask for different things from a tutor, and treating them as one service is how tutoring goes wrong.

In the Primary Years Programme, covering ages three to twelve, the risk is over-correction. Inquiry-led classrooms reward children who ask questions and follow them, and a tutor who converts that into daily worksheets undoes the point of it. Useful support at this stage looks like reading fluency, number sense, and helping a child articulate what they noticed and why it surprised them.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where most parents first feel lost. Marks arrive against criteria A to D rather than a percentage, and a student can understand the science perfectly while scoring poorly because the response never addressed the criterion strand. Tutoring here is largely translation work: reading the task-specific clarification with the student until they can plan an answer against it before writing a word.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, brings the internal assessment, the extended essay, theory of knowledge and terminal papers. Support means IA structure, EE mentoring, TOK argument work, past-paper revision, review of school assignments, and a plan pointing at the May 2026 or November 2026 session.

Younger Diploma cohorts benefit from starting that planning earlier than they expect to.
items: PYP: reading, number sense, inquiry that stays inquiry
MYP: criteria A to D and task-specific clarifications
DP: IA, EE, TOK, command terms and past papers
Concept-based learning respected rather than replaced
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions planned backwards

contentBlocks.heading: Home sessions, online sessions, and the travel arithmetic across Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Distance is measured from your home address, not from the school gate, and that single detail changes the answer for most families.

Home tutoring works well where the tutor already lives or teaches nearby and where the session sits outside the worst of the traffic. A four thirty slot in DLF Phase 1 is a different proposition from a seven thirty slot that requires crossing Sohna Road on a weekday. Home sessions suit younger students, families who want a parent within earshot, and subjects where a tutor needs to see rough working spread across a desk rather than compressed into a screen.

Online tutoring is not the compromise it was once treated as. For a rare higher level subject, for a specialist who happens to live elsewhere in the country, or for revision that has to happen at nine in the evening after a match or a rehearsal, it is often the stronger option. Sharing a past paper and annotating it live is genuinely close to how an examiner reads a script.

The honest limitation: online rarely suits a student who will not switch the camera on, or who needs an adult physically present to stay on task. Some families run a hybrid week, one session at home and one online, which handles both problems reasonably well.

Online preferred for rare HL subjects and late evenings

contentBlocks.heading: Where Pathways World School students most often ask for subject help
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics accounts for the largest share of requests, split between Math AA HL and Math AI HL. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and proof, so tutoring tends to focus on calculus technique and on setting out working that earns method marks even when the final answer slips. Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling and data, so the work is often about reading a context correctly and defending a model rather than choosing the prettiest one.

Physics support usually splits in two: getting the mechanics and fields base solid, then practising the multi-step Paper 2 questions where marks disappear halfway along a long chain of reasoning. Chemistry requests cluster around organic mechanisms, equilibrium, and the internal assessment, particularly the problem of designing an investigation with a variable that can actually be controlled in a school laboratory.

Economics work is mostly diagram discipline and evaluation. A student who can draw a correctly labelled diagram and then write two paragraphs of real evaluation tends to move up a band faster than one who has memorised more definitions. English A requests centre on the individual oral and the comparative essay, where knowing a text well is never the same skill as building an argument about it.

A tutor will say plainly if a subject sits outside what they teach well.

Math AI HL: modelling choices defended in context
Physics: long multi-step Paper 2 chains
Chemistry: mechanisms, equilibrium, controllable IA variables
Economics diagrams and evaluation paragraphs
English A oral commentary and comparative essay work

contentBlocks.heading: Other IB schools around Gurugram, and what a school name tells a tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Gurugram carries a dense cluster of international schools, and families comparing them often ask whether a tutor should have taught at the same school. The honest answer is that it matters less than parents expect.

What a school name genuinely signals is local rhythm: when internal deadlines fall, how long the school day runs, how heavy the co-curricular load is in a given term, and roughly when mocks are scheduled. That rhythm shapes the tutoring plan. It does not change the syllabus, the command terms or the marking criteria, which stay the same wherever the student sits the paper.

Among the schools in this region are Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57, and GD Goenka World School in the Sohna Road region, alongside Pathways World School. Families from several of these live in the same few residential pockets, which is why tutor availability tends to cluster geographically rather than by school.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. It is not officially affiliated with any of the schools listed above, is not endorsed by them, and does not represent them. School names appear here only to describe the local context a tutor will be working within.

contentBlocks.heading: Which parts of Gurugram home tutoring realistically reaches
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and the communities around them, depending entirely on tutor schedules in a given week.

Golf Course Road, taking in Sector 53, Sector 54 and the Rapid Metro corridor, is the easiest belt to staff because tutors already travel it for other students. DLF Phase 5, around The Crest and DLF Park Place, sits on the same corridor and behaves similarly. Sector 57, beside Sushant Lok 3 and Golf Course Extension Road, is well covered though the early evening slots fill first. Sohna Road, near Vatika Chowk and Sectors 49 and 50, is workable in the afternoon and harder once office traffic builds.

Requests also come regularly from Nirvana Country, South City 1, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4, Sector 50 and Sector 65. These sit close enough to the main corridors that a tutor already teaching there can often add a slot without much difficulty.

Some families commute in from Delhi, Noida or Faridabad, or have one parent working there. For them, online sessions usually solve a problem home tutoring cannot: the lesson stops depending on whose car is where at six in the evening.

contentBlocks.heading: What honest tutoring sounds like when nobody can promise a 7
contentBlocks.body:
Anyone promising a specific final grade is not being straight with you. Grade boundaries shift between sessions, examiners vary, and the student still has to write the paper on the day. Treat that promise as a reason to walk away rather than a reason to sign.

What can be described is process. A reasonable tutor will tell you what they intend to cover over the next month, what evidence they will use to judge progress, and what the student is expected to do between sessions. Four weeks in, you should be able to see three concrete things: a marked piece of work carrying fewer of the same errors, a student who can explain a method rather than reproduce it, and a plan for the next month that has changed in response to what happened in the first.

If none of those exist after four weeks, the arrangement is not working, and the right response is to change it rather than wait for the exams to settle the question.

Fees depend on level, subject and mode, and a higher level Diploma subject with a small pool of specialists costs more than a Middle Years session. Ask for the rate and the cancellation terms in writing before the second session. A tutor who is vague about money is often vague about deadlines too.
items: No promised grades, scores or point improvements
A stated plan for the coming month, in writing
Four-week review against marked work, not impressions
Rates and cancellation terms agreed early
Permission to end an arrangement that is not working

contentBlocks.heading: What gets checked before a tutor is introduced to your child
contentBlocks.body:
Screening covers four areas, and each one exists because of a way tutoring commonly fails.

Identity and background come first. Government identity is verified, contact details are confirmed, and references are sought where a tutor has taught previously. That is the baseline for anyone entering a family home.

Subject and level evidence comes second. A claim to teach Math AA HL has to be supported by qualifications and by teaching history at that level. Tutors are asked how they would approach a specific higher level topic, because a confident answer about content is easy to give and a confident answer about how students misunderstand it is not.

Assessment literacy is third. Familiarity with internal assessment criteria, extended essay supervision, theory of knowledge argument and command-term language is treated as a competence separate from subject knowledge. Plenty of strong subject teachers have never marked against these criteria.

Fourth is conduct in session. Feedback from families is reviewed, and repeated lateness, cancelled sessions or an inability to explain progress is taken seriously.

No screening process is perfect, which is exactly why the trial session and the four-week review exist. Screening reduces risk. The review catches what screening misses.
items: Government identity verified and contacts confirmed
Qualifications matched to the exact level claimed
Assessment literacy treated as a separate skill
Session conduct and punctuality reviewed on feedback
Screening backed by a trial and a four-week check

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with an IB tutor near Pathways World School
contentBlocks.body:
The most useful first message is short and specific. Year group, subjects with their levels, whether the need is one subject or a full timetable, the two or three time windows that genuinely work in your week, and whether you would rather begin with home or online sessions.

If mock papers or marked assignments exist, mention them. A tutor who has seen a marked script before the trial can spend that first hour on the actual gap instead of on discovery.

An advisor then goes through the requirement, checks who is currently free at that level, and comes back with a short list rather than a catalogue. Availability is confirmed at that point and not before, because a tutor free this month may not be free next month.

From there a trial session is arranged at a time you choose. You decide afterwards whether to continue, ask for a different tutor, or leave it there. Nothing is locked in before the trial, and there is no expectation that a first match will always be the right one.

If you are still comparing options, it is fine to say that too. An advisor can talk through whether the need is genuinely a tutor, or whether a fortnightly check-in on deadlines would do more for the student this term.
items: Share year group, subjects and levels upfront
Name two or three workable weekly windows
Send marked work or mock scripts if available
Shortlist first, trial session second, decision third
Availability confirmed at the time of matching

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who have taught at Pathways World School?
faqs.answer: Tutor backgrounds vary and availability changes month to month, so no fixed claim is made about any particular school. More usefully, prior teaching at the same school matters less than parents assume. The syllabus, the command terms and the marking criteria are identical wherever a student sits the papers. What a school-aware tutor adds is knowledge of the internal deadline rhythm and the mock timetable, and that context can be shared in the first conversation even by a tutor who has never worked there.

faqs.question: My child has a strong predicted grade but weak mock results. Which one should I act on?
faqs.answer: Act on the mocks, because they are the closest available proxy for an examined paper written under time pressure. A predicted grade blends coursework, class performance and teacher judgement, all of which are real, none of which replicate a two-hour paper. Start by having the mock script read properly. Very often the difference comes down to timing, question selection or command-term handling rather than missing knowledge, and that is fixable within a term if the work starts early enough.

faqs.question: How early should a Middle Years student start preparing for the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Grade 9 and Grade 10 are the sensible years for building habits, though there is no need to touch Diploma content that early. What helps is writing to criteria properly, keeping a clean record of method in mathematics, and getting comfortable with sustained independent research before the extended essay makes it compulsory. Students who reach the Diploma already able to plan an answer against a criterion lose far less time in the first term working out how they are being marked.

faqs.question: What does an internal assessment tutor actually do, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor helps narrow the research question, checks that the method is workable, explains what each criterion is asking for, and gives feedback on drafts much as a teacher would. The line is authorship. The tutor does not write sections, does not supply data, and does not edit the work into something the student could not have produced alone. Schools run authenticity checks and a supervisor conversation, so ghostwritten work tends to surface. Honest IA support is coaching, not co-writing.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring around Golf Course Road and Sohna Road practical on weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on the slot. Afternoon sessions between roughly four and six work reasonably well across Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 5 and Sector 57. Later slots that require crossing Sohna Road or Golf Course Extension Road during peak movement are harder to staff and more likely to be rescheduled. Families in Nirvana Country, South City 1 and Sector 65 often have better luck at weekends. If your only reliable window is late evening, online is the more dependable choice.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition cost, and why do rates differ so much?
faqs.answer: Rates depend on level, subject, mode and how far a tutor travels. Higher level Diploma sciences and Math AA HL sit at the upper end because fewer tutors teach them well. Middle Years and Primary Years sessions cost less. Online is often slightly lower because travel time drops out of the calculation. Exact figures are confirmed with the tutor before you commit, and it is entirely reasonable to ask about cancellation terms and notice periods in the same conversation.

faqs.question: What happens if my child does not get along with the tutor?

contentBlocks.heading: Comparing two tutors for a Scottish High International School student
contentBlocks.body:
Most families end up choosing between two people who both look reasonable on paper. Both hold a good degree. Both say they teach the Diploma Programme. Neither profile tells you which one will make a difference by December.

Four things separate them, and none of them appear on a CV. The first is whether the tutor teaches towards the assessment criteria or towards a textbook chapter. The second is whether work is set between sessions and then actually checked, rather than mentioned and forgotten. The third is how fast the tutor can name the specific thing your child keeps getting wrong, which a strong one usually manages inside two sessions. The fourth is scheduling: a brilliant tutor whose only free hour is nine on a Wednesday night is worse than a good tutor free on Sunday morning.

Families in and around Sector 57 tend to arrive with three requests. Diploma exam revision, usually starting later than it should. Writing support in English and the humanities, where the content is understood but the argument never lands. And mathematics foundations, quietly cracked somewhere in Grade 9, now surfacing under higher level pressure.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. It has no affiliation with Scottish High International School and does not act on the school's behalf.

contentBlocks.heading: Diploma revision, humanities writing and repaired Math foundations in Sector 57
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from this part of Gurugram cluster into three shapes, and each needs a different kind of tutor.

Exam revision for the Diploma is the most common. It usually means past papers under timed conditions, then a slow walk back through the mark scheme to see where marks were available and were not taken. Physics and Chemistry candidates lose most of theirs in extended-response questions. Economics candidates lose them by writing description where the command term asked for evaluation, and by leaving diagrams unlabelled.

Writing support in English A and the humanities is the second shape. Students here are often articulate in conversation and much weaker on paper, because an argument spoken aloud can wander and still convince, while a written one cannot. Work tends to focus on thesis statements, on using textual evidence in support rather than decoration, and on the individual oral where a candidate has to sustain a line of thinking about two texts without notes to lean on.

Mathematics foundations form the third. A Math AA HL student struggling with calculus is frequently a student whose algebraic manipulation was never automatic. Repairing that is unglamorous, takes six to eight weeks, and pays for itself. Math AI HL cases more often need modelling judgement and confident use of technology.

contentBlocks.heading: Five questions that separate a real match from a plausible one
contentBlocks.body:
Ask these in the first conversation, before any money changes hands. They take ten minutes and they filter well.

One. Which levels have you taught in the last two years. A tutor who taught standard level three years ago is a different proposition from one currently teaching higher level, because paper style and emphasis drift.

Two. How would you start with a student who understands the topic but scores badly. If the answer is more practice, keep looking. If the answer involves reading their script and comparing it against the mark scheme, that is the right instinct.

Three. What will you set between sessions, and how will you check it. Vagueness here predicts a term of pleasant, useless conversation.

Four. What do you expect me to see in four weeks. A tutor willing to be specific is a tutor willing to be measured.

Five. Which parts of this subject do you not teach. Anyone claiming to be equally strong across every option topic is overselling.

IB Gram runs the first pass of this filtering during intake, then puts forward two or three profiles with levels taught and current availability, which stays subject to tutor schedules. The trial session is where the remaining questions get answered.

contentBlocks.heading: Primary inquiry to Diploma papers: what support looks like at each stage
contentBlocks.body:
Support is available from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the transitions between programmes cause more difficulty than the programmes themselves.

The Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, builds children who ask good questions. The move into the Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, then asks them to structure those questions into assessed work, and that is where confident young readers sometimes stall. Tutoring at this point is about planning and organisation more than content.

The second transition, from the Middle Years into the Diploma Programme for ages sixteen to nineteen, is sharper. Assessment stops being purely criterion-based coursework and adds terminal papers, subject-specific internal assessments, an extended essay of substantial length, and theory of knowledge, which asks a fifteen-year-old habit of mind to become a seventeen-year-old one. Students who coasted through the Middle Years on natural ability tend to feel this first.

Diploma support covers internal assessment structure, extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge argument, past-paper revision, review of school assignments, and a term plan that works backwards from the May 2026 or November 2026 session. Concept-based learning and command-term language are respected throughout, since a tutor who ignores them teaches a different course from the one being examined.
